reason: Both plans satisfy the hard requirements, but B sequences the work more soundly: it backs up production and notifies stakeholders before any production-side replication setup begins, whereas A configures logical replication/CDC on the production primary (step 2) before either the stakeholder notification (step 3) or the verified backup (step 4) — a real risk since enabling logical replication often requires a wal_level change and restart, i.e. an unannounced production-impacting change. B's dry run also validates the full procedure on a clone before touching production replication, giving a cleaner validate-then-execute flow.
